parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آفرین (āferīn, “well done”), from Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (āferīn, “well done”), from Persian آفرین (âfarin, “bravo”), from Middle Persian 𐭠𐭯𐭥𐭩𐭭 (āfrīn, “praise, blessing”)

parole.significato: dervish, an itinerant Sufi mystic practicing voluntary poverty in devotion to God
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish درویش (derviş), from Persian درویش (darviš), from Middle Persian dlgwš (driyōš, “poor, needy”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فرشته (ferişteh, “angel”) (whence also ferişte, of the same meaning), from Persian فرشته (farišta, ferešte, “angel”). The unetymological final -h is due to the many other words of Persian origin ending in the sound.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كلید (ḱilid), from Persian کلید (kelid), from Middle Persian *kilēd, from Ancient Greek κλείς (kleís), from Proto-Hellenic *klāwī́ds, from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂u-.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كار (kâr), borrowed from Persian کار (kâr), from Middle Persian [script needed] (kʾl /⁠kār⁠/, “work, deed, affair”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷer- (“to do, make, construct”).

From Ottoman Turkish نیلوفر (nîlûfer), from Persian نیلوفر (nilufar), from Middle Persian nylw(k)pl (nīlōpal, “lotus, water-lily”), from Sanskrit नीलोत्पल (nīlotpala, “blue lotus”), from नील (nīla, “blue”) + उत्पल (utpala, “lotus, water-lily”).

parole.significato: idol (object or thing of spiritual worship)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish بت (but) (also vulgar پوت (put)), from Persian بت (“idol”), from Middle Persian bwt' (“Buddha, idol”), ultimately from Sanskrit बुद्ध (buddha).
From Ottoman Turkish سروی (servi), from Persian سرو (sarv), from Middle Persian 𐫘𐫡𐫇 (srw /⁠sarw⁠/, “cypress”).

parole.significato: A wheel-shaped piece of machinery, like a cogwheel or a gear.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish چرخ (çark, “wheel; machine”), from Persian چرخ (čarx), from Middle Persian 𐫝𐫍𐫡 (chr /⁠čahr⁠/, “wheel, cycle”), from Proto-Iranian *čaxrám, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čakrám, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷékʷlos (“wheel, circle”). Doublet of çakra.

From Persian چهره, from Middle Persian 𐭰𐭧𐭫𐭪𐭩 (čihrag), from Old Persian *čiθrakah, from Proto-Iranian *čiθrákah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čitrás, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷi-tróm, from *kʷey- (“bright, burning”).

From Ottoman Turkish شكر (şeker), from Classical Persian شکر (šakar), from Sanskrit शर्करा (śárkarā, “ground or candied sugar", originally "grit, gravel”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱorkeh₂ (“gravel, boulder”). Compare English sugar. Doublet of sakkaroz.
